\[
B_c = c\, \operatorname{clamp}\left(\frac{Y - t}{1 - t}\right),
\quad
c' = c + k\, (G_\sigma * B_c),
\qquad t = \frac{ 70 }{100},\ \sigma = 12,\ k = \frac{ 80 }{100}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(c\): A channel in linear light, from 0 to 1
- \(Y\): The linear luminance
- \(t, \sigma, k\): The threshold, the glow size and the strength

c is a channel in linear light and Y the linear luminance 0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B. The bright part B keeps the share of the light above the threshold, rising linearly from 0 at t to all of it at 1. It is blurred with a Gaussian cut at 3 sigma and added back with the strength k. Light adds in linear space, so the glow mixes with the image as real light would. The results are clipped when encoded. The rule is PixelNexus's own.
